name: AutoBoost SEO – AI Alt Text Generator & Bulk Image SEO
author: Lewis

sections.description:
AutoBoost SEO connects your WordPress site to the AutoBoost SEO web app, where AI writes missing alt text for the images in your posts, hundreds at a time. You review each change before it is saved, and the alt text goes into both the post and your media library. The free plugin also runs an SEO audit inside WordPress, and the app’s free plan includes AI alt text on 5 posts a month.

It fixes missing meta descriptions, SEO titles and focus keywords the same way, instead of editing posts one at a time.

Start with a free SEO audit. The plugin scans every published post right inside WordPress, with no account needed, and shows your overall SEO health: how many posts are missing a meta description, an SEO title or a focus keyword, how many have images with missing alt text, and which posts need the most work. The audit runs entirely on your own server. Nothing leaves your site until you choose to fix something.

Then fix the gaps in bulk. When you are ready, one click hands the work to the AutoBoostSEO platform, which generates optimised meta descriptions, SEO titles and focus keywords across hundreds or thousands of pages at once, and saves them straight into Rank Math or Yoast SEO. You review and approve every change before anything is saved, and every change keeps an undo copy of what it replaced.

Works with your existing SEO plugin. AutoBoost saves SEO titles, meta descriptions and focus keywords into Rank Math and Yoast SEO. The audit also reads All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework, but AutoBoost cannot save into those three plugins yet. It complements the SEO plugin you already run rather than replacing it.

Built for large sites. The connector is optimised for libraries with tens of thousands of posts, using fast bulk endpoints so both the audit and the fixes stay quick at scale.

What you get:

  • Bulk AI alt text for the images in your posts and their featured images, saved to the post and the media library
  • A free, in-dashboard SEO audit of every post, with no account required, including posts with images missing alt text
  • Bulk AI generation of missing meta descriptions, SEO titles and focus keywords
  • A clear view of your lowest-scoring posts, fixed across the whole site at once
  • One-click connection to AutoBoostSEO, with no API keys or copy-paste
  • Saves to Rank Math and Yoast SEO; the audit also reads All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework
  • WooCommerce products: SEO titles, meta descriptions, focus keywords and image alt text
  • An undo copy of the last 3 AutoBoost changes on each post, and an Undo button in the app
  • Built-in connection diagnostics to troubleshoot any issues

Create a free account at autoboostseo.com when you are ready to fix what the audit finds.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin via Plugins → Add New → Upload, or search “AutoBoostSEO” in the plugin directory.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. That’s it – no settings to configure.
sections.faq:
Do I need an AutoBoostSEO account?

Yes. You’ll need a free or paid account at autoboostseo.com. The plugin connects your WordPress site to the AutoBoostSEO platform.

Which SEO plugins does it support?

AutoBoost saves SEO titles, meta descriptions and focus keywords into Rank Math and Yoast SEO. The free audit also reads All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework, but AutoBoost cannot save into those three plugins yet. The plugin detects which one you are using.

Will this plugin slow down my site?

No. The connector runs lightweight background tasks and is optimized for performance, even on sites with tens of thousands of posts.

How can I troubleshoot connection issues?

Use the built-in diagnostic tool available in the WordPress admin. It checks API access, authentication, and plugin compatibility.

Is there a free tier?

Yes. The free plan includes 5 AI credits a month (one credit per post), so you can write AI alt text for the images on 5 posts a month, or fix 5 meta descriptions or SEO titles. Paid plans add more credits, bigger bulk runs and more sites.

Can I undo a change AutoBoost made?

Yes. Before AutoBoost overwrites a title, excerpt, URL slug or SEO field, it keeps the old value in a hidden custom field on the post (_autoboostseo_backup, the last 3 changes, size-limited). For WooCommerce products, which have no WordPress revisions, and on sites that turn revisions off, it also keeps the old content. Use “Undo last AutoBoost change” in the app to put it back; it refuses if the post was edited since. Otherwise post and page content changes are in WordPress’s own revisions.

What data does the plugin send to AutoBoostSEO?

On activation and on upgrade, the plugin sends a one-time, non-blocking ping to https://www.autoboostseo.com/api/install-ping containing: a random install ID generated locally on activation, your site URL, the plugin version, WordPress version, PHP version, locale, and whether the site is multisite. No post content, no admin email, no personally identifiable information is included. This helps us measure how many installs of the WordPress.org plugin lead to active accounts so we can prioritise improvements. No further pings are sent at runtime.

What data is exchanged when I click Connect?

When you click Connect your site, the plugin opens https://www.autoboostseo.com/connect with your install ID and your site URL in the URL, plus a one-time pairing code in the part after the # (browsers do not send that part to servers). Your site stores only a hash of the code, and accepts it once, within 15 minutes. You sign in with Google. AutoBoostSEO then posts a signed pairing token back to your WordPress site, which the plugin stores in wp_options (the raw token is hashed before storage; your AutoBoostSEO email and user ID are stored in plain text so the plugin can show you who the site is paired with). At the same time, the plugin generates a WordPress Application Password scoped to your primary administrator account (named “AutoBoostSEO Connector”) and relays it to AutoBoostSEO so the SaaS can call your site’s REST API without further configuration. AutoBoostSEO stores this credential in your account settings document on Firestore. A paired_sites record is also created containing your install ID, site URL, AutoBoostSEO user ID and email, paired timestamp, and token hash. You can disconnect at any time from either the plugin’s admin page or the AutoBoostSEO dashboard. Disconnecting, or deleting the plugin, revokes that Application Password; you can also see and revoke it yourself in your WordPress profile under Users → Profile → Application Passwords.
sections.changelog:
5.9.8

  • Security: connecting a site now needs a one-time code from your WordPress admin page, and disconnecting or deleting the plugin revokes its application password.

5.9.7

  • NEW: The SEO Audit counts posts with images missing alt text. A new read-only endpoint, GET /wp-json/autoboost/v1/missing-alt-counts, counts images with a missing or empty alt per post (needs the edit_posts capability and only counts posts the user may read; at most 100 posts a request, time-limited, returns counts only). It never changes post content; counts are cached in hidden post meta (_autoboostseo_alt_counts) by each post’s modified time and removed on uninstall.
  • NEW: Undo copy. Hidden post meta _autoboostseo_backup (all public post types, edit context only, editors only) keeps the values AutoBoost overwrote, last 3 changes, size-limited; the app writes it in the same request as the change and can restore it. A read-only REST field, autoboostseo_revisions (edit context), tells the app whether WordPress keeps revisions for the post, so content is copied too when it does not.
  • NEW: WooCommerce products can be opened by the app. When WooCommerce is active and the product type is not in the REST API, the plugin turns that on (show_in_rest) and keeps the product screen in the editor it already used.
  • NEW: A one-time review request on the AutoBoost admin page only, for administrators, after the site has been connected for 7 days. Leave a review or dismiss it once and it never shows again for you.
  • Listing: says plainly that AutoBoost saves into Rank Math and Yoast SEO (the audit also reads All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework), and that the free plan includes AI alt text on 5 posts a month.

5.9.6

  • Listing: leads with bulk AI alt text, which the AutoBoost SEO app now saves into your posts and media library. No plugin code changes.

5.9.5

  • FIX: The SEO Audit “Fix with AI” and “Continue with Google” buttons now always carry your install ID and site details, so signing in connects your site straight away instead of dropping you on a blank sign-in page.

5.9.4

  • IMPROVED: The SEO Audit is now the first thing you see when you open AutoBoostSEO (previously a separate submenu). Connection and settings now sit below the audit on the same page.

5.9.3

  • NEW: Free SEO Audit page. A new “SEO Audit” screen under the AutoBoostSEO menu scans every published post locally — no account needed — and shows your site SEO health, how many posts are missing meta descriptions, SEO titles and focus keywords, and the posts that need the most work. One-click “Fix with AI” hands off to AutoBoostSEO. Runs entirely against the plugin’s own REST API; no data leaves your server until you choose to fix something.

5.9.1

  • IMPROVED: Plugin directory listing — clearer, benefit-led title, short description, long description and search tags so the right users can find the plugin. No functional or code changes.

5.9.0

  • NEW: Tier-aware pairing. The SaaS now blocks OAuth pairs that would push your account over its plan’s site limit and shows a clear “upgrade or remove a site” prompt on the connect page instead of silently exceeding quota.
  • NEW: Subsequent pairs no longer hijack the active site. If you already have a connected site selected in AutoBoostSEO, pairing another one adds it without switching your dashboard away from what you were working on.
  • NEW: Periodic pair-health probe. Once per hour, while you’re in wp-admin, the plugin checks whether the SaaS still considers this site paired. If you disconnected from the AutoBoostSEO dashboard, the plugin clears its local pair state automatically and surfaces a one-time admin notice so you can reconnect — no more “both ends think they’re paired” divergence.

5.8.0

  • NEW: Pairing now auto-provisions a WordPress Application Password (named “AutoBoostSEO Connector”) for the site’s primary administrator and relays it to AutoBoostSEO inside the same /pair callback. AutoBoostSEO writes it into your account settings so the rest of the app (content browse, AI enhancement) works against the paired site immediately — no manual Application Password setup. Plain credential never persists locally; only WP’s own bcrypt-hashed copy remains in wp_users meta.
  • NEW: /pair response now includes site_name, seo_plugin (auto-detected), and the WP admin username so the SaaS can pre-fill the connection settings on its side.
  • IMPROVED: privacy FAQ updated to disclose the Application Password generation.

5.7.0

  • NEW: One-click WordPress pairing. The plugin’s hero card now has a “Connect your site” button that opens AutoBoostSEO, walks you through Google sign-in, and pairs your site automatically. No passwords, no API keys, no copy-paste. The paired account email is shown in the admin once connected, with a Disconnect link.
  • NEW: REST endpoint POST /wp-json/autoboost/v1/pair receives the pairing token from AutoBoostSEO. Three-layer auth: HMAC over install_id|token|ts using a shared secret, ±5-minute timestamp window, and install_id match against the local installation. Permission-callback is open by design (AutoBoostSEO has no WP credentials); HMAC + token + install_id is the proof.
  • NEW: REST endpoint GET /wp-json/autoboost/v1/pair-status reports the local pair state for the admin UI (manage_options-gated).
  • NEW: admin-AJAX action autoboostseo_disconnect_pair tears down the pair from the WP admin. POSTs an HMAC-signed disconnect to AutoBoostSEO and clears the local options.
  • IMPROVED: privacy FAQ updated to disclose pairing data.

5.6.0

  • NEW: Prominent “Create your free account” CTA at the top of the plugin admin page so new installs can sign up without leaving WordPress.
  • NEW: Outbound links to autoboostseo.com are now UTM-tagged (utm_source=wp-plugin) so we can measure how many plugin users reach the website.
  • NEW: One-time, non-blocking install/upgrade ping to www.autoboostseo.com/api/install-ping with anonymous install ID, site URL, and version numbers. Lets us measure plugin install → account signup conversion. See FAQ for the exact payload.
  • IMPROVED: Admin page step list now reflects the real onboarding flow (install → sign up → connect) instead of just pointing at the connection test.

5.5.3

  • Tested with WordPress 7.0
  • Improved plugin listing for better discovery and clarity
  • Added FAQ section with common user questions
  • Added Screenshots section with placeholder descriptions

5.5.2

  • FIX: Wrap all SQL queries in $wpdb->prepare() for WordPress.org plugin review compliance

5.4.3

  • DEBUG: Public diagnostic endpoint for score filter debugging (temporary)

5.4.1

  • FIX: Low SEO score filter no longer crashes when no posts have been scored yet

5.4.0

  • NEW: Plugin-side SEO score calculation — computes and stores scores as _autoboostseo_score post meta, independent of RankMath/Yoast stored scores
  • NEW: GET /autoboost/v1/scores-status endpoint — returns scoring index status
  • NEW: POST /autoboost/v1/calculate-scores endpoint — batch scores unscored posts (200/batch)
  • IMPROVED: Low SEO score filter now uses plugin-calculated scores for reliable filtering and global sort order
  • IMPROVED: Posts-metadata endpoint now includes _autoboostseo_score in response
  • FIX: SEO scores auto-calculated on post save (save_post hook)

5.3.3

  • FIX: Server-side filter pagination broken on page 2+ (WP_Query applied double offset on post__in results). All filters affected.
  • FEATURE: Low SEO score filter now sorts results by score ascending (lowest first).

5.3.2

  • FIX: SEO stats endpoint now includes pages in addition to posts. Previously only counted post_type=’post’, missing pages entirely.

5.3.1

  • FIX: Posts with the same date now appear in consistent order between paginated and Show All views. Added p.ID DESC as secondary sort to all SQL queries.

5.3.0

  • FEATURE: posts-metadata endpoint accepts limit parameter. Frontend passes tier limit so the plugin stops returning posts early (e.g. 7500 instead of 21094 for Starter tier). Cuts Show All load time by ~60%.

5.2.5

  • FIX: Word count filter now works server-side even without full backfill. Uses COALESCE to treat unindexed posts as 0 words instead of excluding them. No more loading all 21k posts for word count filtering.

5.2.4

  • FIX: Server-side filters with status=any only returned published posts. WP REST API passes status as array [‘any’], not string ‘any’, so the previous string check failed silently. Now uses in_array() to detect ‘any’ in the status array and expands to all allowed statuses.

5.2.3

  • FIX: (Incomplete) Initial attempt at status=any fix — used is_string() check which doesn’t work because WP REST API passes status as an array.

5.2.2

  • FIX: Removed bulk word count auto-compute from metadata endpoint. do_shortcode() on 1000 posts per page was causing server timeouts on large sites, making the fast endpoint fall back to slow 100-per-page standard API.
  • FIX: Reduced backfill batch size from 500 to 50 to safely handle do_shortcode() per post.

5.2.1

  • FIX: Word count now computed from rendered content (shortcodes expanded via do_shortcode before counting). Previously raw shortcode syntax was stripped, causing posts with galleries/embeds/shortcodes to show artificially low word counts. A post that renders as 800 words on the site was counted as ~50.
  • AUTO: Word count index automatically rebuilt on upgrade.

5.2.0

  • FIX: Word count computation now consistent between SQL filter and REST API display. Previously strip_shortcodes() caused server-side word counts to be lower than displayed values, making word count filters return wrong results.
  • FIX: Conflicting filter pairs (e.g. Missing Keywords + Has Keywords) now return 0 results immediately with a clear response instead of running expensive SQL that always returns nothing.
  • FIX: Inverted word count ranges (min > max) handled gracefully on server.
  • AUTO: Existing word count index is automatically rebuilt on upgrade to match the corrected algorithm.

5.1.3

  • PERF: posts-metadata endpoint now computes and stores word counts on-the-fly for unindexed posts using bulk SQL (2 queries per 1000 posts). Word count filtering is now accurate from first use without requiring a separate backfill step.

5.1.2

  • FIX: posts-metadata endpoint now includes the post permalink (link field) so posts are clickable in the app.

5.1.1

  • FIX: posts-metadata endpoint now returns posts ordered newest to oldest (post_date DESC). Previously returned in ID order.
  • FIX: posts-metadata endpoint now fetches posts only (excludes pages) by default.

5.1.0

  • NEW: Bulk posts-metadata endpoint (GET /autoboost/v1/posts-metadata) — returns 1000 posts/page vs 100, using a single optimised SQL query per page. Reduces Show All load time from ~3.5 minutes to ~15 seconds on large sites (21k+ posts). Supports RankMath, Yoast, SEOPress, TSF, and AIOSEO.

5.0.1

  • CLEANUP: Removed dead REST fields (thin_content, long_content, has_schema, missing_schema, reading_time)
  • These fields were never used by the frontend and added unnecessary overhead to API responses

5.0.0

  • MAJOR: All filters now use raw SQL with LEFT JOIN for correct pagination at any scale
  • NEW: SEOPress support (focus keyword, SEO title, meta description)
  • NEW: The SEO Framework support (title, description)
  • NEW: All in One SEO (AIOSEO) full support via wp_aioseo_posts table
  • NEW: missing_title filter (posts with empty titles)
  • NEW: word_count_min/word_count_max filters (requires word count indexing)
  • NEW: comment_count_min/comment_count_max filters
  • NEW: default_seo_title filter now correctly compares SEO title to post title
  • NEW: Word count computed and stored as post_meta on save (backfill endpoint available)
  • FIX: Filters now respect post_type and post_status from request (no longer hardcoded to post/publish)
  • FIX: SEO score filters include unscored posts in low_seo_score results
  • FIX: found_posts filter no longer leaks to other WP_Query calls
  • FIX: filter-debug endpoint now requires authentication
  • FIX: N+1 query problem eliminated via postmeta cache priming
  • FIX: Version constant mismatch between class and define
  • REMOVED: Legacy query handler (class-query-handler.php) — conflicting dual filter system
  • REMOVED: Dead filter params (thin_content, long_content, reading_time_min/max)
  • REMOVED: update_option debug write on every filtered request
  • PERF: NOT IN subqueries replaced with LEFT JOIN … IS NULL (5-10x faster at 100k+ posts)

4.7.5

  • FIX: Raw SQL paginated approach for SEO filters — bypasses RankMath posts_where stripping
  • Runs raw SQL to get only the current page’s post IDs, then uses tiny post__in (20 IDs)
  • Overrides found_posts for correct REST API pagination headers

4.7.4

  • FIX: Replace post__in (17K+ IDs) with posts_where subqueries for large sites
  • Fixes “No matching posts” when filtering sites with many missing SEO fields

4.7.3

  • FIX: SEO filters now check only the ACTIVE plugin’s fields (reverts 4.7.2 all-variants approach)
  • Residual Yoast data no longer causes false negatives when RankMath is active
  • Dashboard seo-stats endpoint now uses raw SQL (consistent with REST filters, bypasses WP_Query NOT EXISTS bug)

4.7.2

  • FIX: SEO filters now check ALL plugin field variants (RankMath + Yoast) regardless of active plugin
  • Fixes incorrect filter results on sites with residual Yoast metadata after switching to RankMath
  • Dashboard stats and content filters now return consistent results

4.7.1

  • Switched ALL SEO filters to raw SQL + post__in approach — bypasses WP_Query meta_query bugs, post__not_in stripping, and RankMath posts_where consumption
  • “Missing” filters now run direct SQL to find missing post IDs, then use post__in to include only those
  • “Has” filters use same approach for consistency and reliability

4.7.0

  • Fixed server-side filters consumed by RankMath sub-queries — replaced self-removing posts_where with persistent filter using custom query var
  • All “missing” filters (keywords, SEO title, meta description) now use autoboost_exclude_ids query var immune to third-party query consumption
  • Both REST controller and query handler updated

4.6.9

  • Fixed ALL server-side filters: replaced post__not_in (stripped by WP REST pipeline) with direct SQL WHERE injection
  • Affects missing keywords, missing SEO title, missing meta description filters for RankMath and dual-plugin setups
  • Both REST controller and query handler updated

4.6.8

  • Added diagnostic logging to REST filter callback to debug post__not_in issue

3.4.6

  • Added filter-debug diagnostic endpoint to troubleshoot server-side filtering
  • Fixed server-side filters using raw SQL instead of nested WP_Meta_Query (workaround for WP Trac #29560)

3.4.4

  • Fixed RankMath meta key variant handling — filters now check both rank_math_* and rank_math* keys
  • Fixed dashboard stats to include non-underscore RankMath meta keys
  • Fixed class VERSION constant (was 3.4.2)

3.4.3

  • Fixed server-side filters returning all posts when only one SEO plugin is installed

3.4

  • Security improvements and bug fixes

3.3

  • Connection diagnostics

3.2

  • Redesigned admin page

3.0

  • Major update with improved performance and filtering

2.0

  • Advanced filtering and better performance

1.0

  • Initial release
